Man charged after June Kenwood shooting that seriously injured a 15-year-old boy
articles.description:
A 48-year-old Chicago man has been charged with attempted murder after shooting at three people, including a 15-year-old boy who was seriously wounded in June in the Kenwood neighborhood.

Shauntay Sardin, 48, was charged with three counts of attempted murder because there were two additional victims who were not shot, and aggravated battery, police said.

On June 20 in the 700 block of East 47th Street, Sardin allegedly opened fire at three people, including a 15-year-old boy who was shot and seriously injured, police said.

Sardin, of the 1900 block of East 72nd Place in South Shore and who was arrested Monday in the 5100 block of South Indiana Avenue, was due for a detention hearing Tuesday at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse

articles.title: UN report finds Nicaraguan government responsible for in-custody deaths
articles.description: A U.N. report says the Nicaraguan government is responsible for at least eight deaths in custody since 2018. The report published Tuesday condemns the government of co-Presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo for crushing dissent and canceling elections. It highlights inconsistencies in the death of Indigenous leader Brooklyn Rivera, who died in May after 32 months in prison. The official explanation linked his death to COVID-19 complications, but an independent assessment found this "not medically coherent." The report calls for Rivera’s body to be released for a traditional burial and urges the government to release information on missing detainees.

articles.title: Chicago police fatally shoot dog that attacked them in Humboldt Park
articles.description:
Chicago police shot and killed a dog that attacked them while the officers were working on an investigation in the Humboldt Park neighborhood Monday, police said.

Shortly before 5 p.m., the officers were in the 700 block of North Christiana Avenue when a dog approached and attacked an officer. One of the officers then shot the dog.

The dog died and the city's Department of Animal Care and Control was notified.

Three officers were taken to nearby hospitals in good condition. No other injuries were reported.

Detectives are continuing to investigate the incident.

articles.title: 2 helicopter pilots killed while making water drops on Yosemite fire
articles.description: The Dome fire burning in Yosemite national park on 15 September. Photograph: National Parks Service/AP Two helicopter pilots died while fighting a fire in Yosemite national park on Sunday afternoon. The pilots were conducting water drops over the Dome fire, which had burned more than 3,000 acres since it ignited last week, when their helicopter crashed around 3pm, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Related: ‘We’re near a breaking point:’ firefighters say US government is failing them amid intense wildfire season The pilots were employed by the aerospace company Precision and were working with a wildland firefighting crew that specializes in using ropes to descend from helicopters to reach otherwise inaccessible terrain, known as helitack rappelling. The helicopter went down southeast of Ostrander Lake, said Benjamin Cossel, a spokesperson with the Federal Complex Incident Management Team overseeing the firefighting response. Details about the circumstances surrounding the crash were not immediately released. The crash will be investigated by the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board. “It is with unimaginable sadness and broken hearts that we share the loss of two beloved members of our team,” Precision wrote in a social media post. “We are devastated by this loss and are struggling to find the words. We ask for privacy and compassion for their families and our team as we grieve this tremendous loss.” The names of the pilots were not immediately released. Roughly 580 people are fighting the Dome Fire, which started on 15 September near Wawona, California, according to the National Interagency Fire Center. It’s burning on about 4.7 sq miles (12.3 sq km) and is about 15% contained. The lake near the crash site was roughly 9 miles (14.5km) south of Yosemite’s iconic El Capitan, and about 7 miles (11.3km) northeast of Wawona. Water-dropping helicopters have been key to fighting the blaze, which has spread across rugged terrain. At least 14 people have died while helping with wildfires in the US this year, the most since 2022 when 25 deaths were recorded, according to government reports. Three firefighters died battling Colorado’s Knowles fire , and an additional member of that crew succumbed to injuries weeks afterwards. The incident was the most deadly entrapment in 13 years. The job has always carried inherent risks,but this year has been especially dangerous. The Trump administration has increased pressure on firefighting forces, amid a critical shortage of federal firefighters.
